title: Magnetic Stirrer / Hot Plate

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: Provides controlled heating and/or continuous stirring of a liquid using a rotating magnetic field that spins a small stir bar inside the vessel, commonly used for dissolving reagents, preparing media/buffers, and maintaining a stirred solution during pH adjustment.
operatingPrinciple: A rotating magnet (or electronically switched magnetic field) beneath the plate surface couples with a coated ferromagnetic stir bar placed inside the liquid, spinning it continuously to mix the contents; many units also include a resistive heating element in the plate surface, controlled independently of the stirring speed.
basicOperation: Place the vessel (with an appropriately sized stir bar inside) on the plate, centered over the stirring mechanism.
Start stirring at a low speed and gradually increase to avoid the stir bar being thrown off-center ('bar walkout').
If heating is needed, set the target temperature and monitor with a thermometer or the plate's own probe if equipped, since surface-set temperature may not equal actual liquid temperature.
Turn off heat and stirring, and allow the plate to cool, before removing the vessel or leaving it unattended.
importantSettings: Stir speed (too high can cause bar walkout or excessive vortexing/splashing)
Heat setting (surface dial temperature is often not the same as actual liquid temperature unless a probe is used)
maintenance: Wipe spilled reagent off the plate surface promptly to prevent buildup and corrosion.
Check stir bars for chipped coating, which can expose the metal core to the solution.

commonErrors.problem: Stir bar stops spinning ('walkout') or spins erratically
commonErrors.cause: Stir speed set too high for the bar size/vessel, or the vessel not centered over the stirring mechanism
commonErrors.fix: Reduce speed, recenter the vessel, or use a larger/more appropriately sized stir bar

commonErrors.problem: Liquid overheats or scorches despite a moderate dial setting
commonErrors.cause: Surface dial temperature does not equal actual liquid temperature, especially without stirring to distribute heat
commonErrors.fix: Use a probe thermometer to monitor actual liquid temperature rather than relying on the dial setting alone, and keep stirring on while heating

safety: Allow the plate surface to cool before handling — it can remain hot well after the heating element is switched off.
Never heat a sealed or closed vessel on a hot plate, since pressure buildup can cause it to rupture.
